title: Software Development Engineer II, AFT Sortation, AFT Mansort
descriptionHtml:
Have you ever wondered how Amazon delivers millions of customer orders with exceptional speed and reliability? Behind every fast and on-time delivery is a complex network of software, infrastructure, robotics, and operational processes engineered to work seamlessly at scale.

Amazon Fulfillment Technologies (AFT) builds the software and infrastructure that power Amazon's world-class fulfillment centers. Our systems integrate with warehouse automation, machines, and human associates to orchestrate critical fulfillment processes across a global network. These technologies enable the movement of millions of inventory units and support billions of transactions, ensuring that customers receive the products they want, when they expect them.

About the Mansort Team

The Mansort team owns the manual sortation layer of Amazon's fulfillment network. Our systems determine where packages should be routed after packing and before reaching the outbound dock, enabling accurate and efficient movement of shipments through fulfillment centers.

We build and operate software responsible for sort plan generation, chute and destination assignment, and scan-and-sort workflows used by warehouse associates. Our systems operate on the fulfillment center floor across hundreds of buildings worldwide, where reliability, performance, and correctness directly influence operational efficiency and customer delivery promises.

Mansort operates in a technically demanding environment characterized by high transaction volumes, stringent low-latency requirements, and the need for continuous availability despite connectivity disruptions or upstream dependency failures. Correctness is equally critical: every sortation decision must accurately direct a package to its intended destination to prevent operational errors and missed transportation cutoffs.

Manual sortation complements Amazon's automated sortation capabilities by providing the flexibility and scalability needed to handle peak demand, support new geographies and fulfillment center formats, and accommodate diverse operational requirements that cannot always be addressed through fixed automation.

As Amazon continues to expand its global fulfillment network and introduce new supply chain capabilities, delivery models, and customer experiences, the Mansort team has an opportunity to solve challenging engineering problems, modernize existing systems, and build scalable, resilient solutions that support the future of fulfillment operations.

Key job responsibilities
Design and develop scalable systems by owning the architecture, design, implementation, testing, and deployment of distributed software systems operating in live fulfillment center environments.

Build high-throughput, low-latency services that meet stringent performance, scalability, and availability requirements.

Ensure operational reliability and correctness through robust sortation workflows, data integrity, routing accuracy, fault tolerance, and graceful degradation.

Solve complex business and technical problems using pragmatic engineering decisions, innovative solutions, and modern technologies.

Drive operational excellence by improving observability, monitoring, troubleshooting, and recovery mechanisms to minimize disruptions.

Collaborate with product managers, operations teams, process engineers, and partner engineering teams to improve fulfillment efficiency and customer experience.

Influence technical direction by contributing to architecture, engineering standards, and technical strategy within the team and broader organization.

Maintain high engineering standards by writing clean, maintainable, well-tested code and ensuring software quality, performance, security, and reliability.

Mentor engineers through knowledge sharing, design discussions, code reviews, and technical guidance to strengthen team capabilities.

Basic qualifications

- 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
- 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
- Experience programming with at least one software programming language

Preferred qualifications

- 3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience
- Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent

title: Device Specialist, Device Management Team (DMT)
descriptionHtml:
Do you love hands-on logistics and working with technology before it hits the shelves? Amazon's Device Management Team (DMT) is looking for a self-motivated Device Specialist to join our Seattle operations, the team that ensures every prototype, beta unit, and production device across Amazon's entire consumer hardware portfolio gets where it needs to go.

- You'll work directly with physical devices daily, packaging, scanning, distributing, and coordinating shipments across buildings and around the world
- You'll support programs like Echo, Kindle, Ring, Fire TV, Eero, and Kuiper from earliest prototypes through mass production
- You'll be part of a small, high-impact team where your work is visible to senior leadership and directly tied to product launch success
- You'll have real ownership, managing your domain end-to-end, solving problems proactively, and building processes that scale as device volume grows
We need someone who thrives in a fast-paced, physical environment, can adapt on the fly when priorities shift, and takes pride in being the person others count on. If you want a role where no two days look the same and the tech in your hands hasn't been announced yet, this is it.

Key job responsibilities
This role requires daily hands-on work with physical devices, packaging, scanning, labeling, and distributing units across multiple buildings on campus. You'll be on your feet, moving between sites to meet program teams, deliver devices, and coordinate pickups throughout the day.

Core responsibilities include:

- Device fulfillment: Process allocation requests, pick and pack devices, prepare shipments, and assemble controlled return kits to meet same-day or next-day deadlines
- Inventory management: Receive incoming devices, scan into tracking systems, audit stock levels, and flag discrepancies before they become problems
- Cross-site coordination: Deliver and collect devices across buildings, coordinating handoffs with program managers and lab teams on tight timelines
- Triage and adaptability: Respond to urgent requests, troubleshoot delivery exceptions, and reprioritize on the fly when launch schedules shift or volume spikes hit
- Process improvement: Identify bottlenecks in day-to-day operations and propose solutions — better labeling systems, smarter routing, streamlined handoff procedures
The ideal candidate is someone who can see around corners, anticipating what's needed before being asked, adapting to shifting priorities, and proactively solving problems rather than waiting for direction. Physical presence and reliability are non-negotiable; our customers depend on devices arriving on time, every time.

A day in the life
Your day starts at standup, syncing with the team on what's shipping, what's arriving, and what needs attention. From there, you're processing device allocation requests, coordinating shipments with program teams, and triaging customer inquiries through SIM tickets. You might prep controlled device return kits, troubleshoot a delivery exception, or update logistics dashboards to keep leadership informed. No two days look the same, volume spikes with product launches and beta builds keep things dynamic. You're equal parts problem-solver, logistics coordinator, and process builder, with real ownership over how Seattle operations run.

About the team
The Device Management Team (DMT) is the operational backbone of Amazon's consumer devices portfolio. We ensure every prototype, test unit, and production device — across Echo, Fire TV, Kindle, Ring, Eero, Kuiper, and more — gets to the right place, at the right time. We're a 10-person team spanning Seattle, Munich, and Chennai who thrive on solving logistics puzzles at scale. Our culture values builders over operators, we invent tools, automate workflows, and own our domains end-to-end. With work visible to high level leadership, the bar is high and the impact is real.

Basic qualifications

- Experience in an operational role

Preferred qualifications

- 2+ years of manufacturing or customer-facing environment experience

title: Senior Manager, Product Management, Technical, Enterprise Foundational AI
descriptionHtml:

We are looking for a Senior Manager, Product Management – Technical to own the product vision, roadmap, and delivery for a portfolio that includes Amazon Quick, AI model routing and orchestration optimization services, and foundational products that accelerate Amazon's shift to an AI-native product development lifecycle. In this role, you will lead a team of product managers and technical program managers through significant ambiguity, deciding which problems to solve, how to sequence investment, and when to pivot. You will partner with engineering, AWS product teams, and functional stakeholders in Security, Legal, and People Experience and Technology (PXT) to ship products that reach every major Amazon business unit. If you want to shape the AI tools that hundreds of thousands of Amazonians rely on every day, we would love to talk.

Key job responsibilities
- Define and communicate the multi-year product vision and strategy for Enterprise Foundational AI's portfolio, translating ambiguous internal customer needs into a prioritized roadmap that balances near-term delivery with long-term platform goals.
- Lead, coach, and grow a team of product managers and technical program managers, setting the hiring bar, developing future leaders, and building an inclusive team culture where people make sound decisions and deliver independently.
- Partner with engineering and applied science teams to develop functional and non-functional requirements, evaluate system design trade-offs around scalability and performance, and determine when to integrate generative AI capabilities to improve product quality and team productivity.
- Drive cross-functional alignment with AWS product teams, Security, Legal, PXT, and major Amazon business units by writing clear strategic narratives and presenting investment cases to senior leadership.
- Establish mechanisms to inspect product quality, operational performance, and the internal customer experience, proactively identifying risks and decomposing complex problems into actionable solutions that scale across the organization.

A day in the life
Your morning might start by reviewing a product narrative from one of your direct reports, sharpening the customer problem statement before a working session with engineering on AI model orchestration trade-offs. After lunch you lead a roadmap prioritization discussion, helping the team weigh competing signals from business units against resource constraints. Later you prepare a strategic update for senior leadership, distilling progress on Amazon Quick adoption into a concise, data-informed story that frames the path forward.

About the team
Enterprise Foundational AI builds the products, layers, and services that put trusted generative AI in the hands of every Amazonian. The team's portfolio spans Amazon Quick, AI model routing and orchestration, and foundational capabilities that are accelerating Amazon's AI-native transformation. As the investment in AI-native products continues to grow, the team is expanding. You will manage product managers and technical program managers, partnering closely with AWS product teams and cross-functional stakeholders across Security, Legal, and PXT. If you are excited about building AI products at a scale few organizations can match, this is the team for you.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree
- 6+ years of team management experience

And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

We have an immediate opening for a Fleet Remediation Project Design Mechanical Engineer in Oregon. If you meet these qualifications, exude passion, and enjoy the challenge of innovative projects at hyper-scale, this job is for you!

As an Amazon Fleet Remediation Project Design Engineer, you will lead design projects in operational data centers, that remediate issues, upgrade our existing infrastructure or add new services. You will be the 'go to' engineering resource for these projects and will provide lifecycle support from design through implementation. You will use your electrical expertise to:

- Act as a technical subject matter expert for your given discipline during new remediation projects.
- Support construction, commissioning, operations, and turnover.

Key job responsibilities
Amazon's vision is to be the world's most customer-centric company, and this role is key to that vision. As a Fleet Remediation Project Design Mechanical Engineer, you will be leading projects to fit out our data centers to meet ever-evolving customer needs as we continue expanding our fleet to hyper-scale. - Possess Strong Engineering Judgement and are able to provide design and recommendations despite uncertainty

title: Senior Maintenance Technician, Amazon Reliability Maintenance Engineering - IntlRME
descriptionHtml:

As Amazon evolves and adapts, this team makes sure that the tools and technologies we use do as well. As a Senior RME Technician, you'll help us stay one step ahead, adopting the latest technologies and identifying new and efficient ways of working. title: Sr. Associate - Quality Analyst, Global Solutions & Risk Compliance (GSRC)
descriptionHtml:
The Global Solutions and Risk Compliance (GSRC) organization is a component of Amazon's operations, dedicated to ensuring the compliance of its products and services worldwide. GSRC's core mission is to keep customers, partners, and associates safe while protecting the company from legal and regulatory risks. With a diverse global team spanning across India, China, Poland, Romania, Netherlands, Jordan, Philippines and Costa Rica, GSRC partners with its stakeholders to classify products and ensure regulatory and legal compliance for product listings. GSRC raises the bar on quality by implementing operational changes matching the everchanging regulatory space. The team designs global, consistent, and scalable solutions and prioritize a blend between technology-driven and human decision-making processes. GSRC believes that innovation thrives on diversity, fostering an inclusive and equitable culture that empowers employees with opportunities for learning and development.

Key job responsibilities
Your job responsibilities as a Sr. Compliance Associate-Quality Analyst may include:
• Performs quality audits on a daily basis using Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) and achieves self-utilization, productivity and quality as per defined targets.
• Must be able to comprehend SOPs with minimal support and identify opportunities.
• Identifies anomalies through audits (SOP defects, Process gaps etc.).
• Uses knowledge and identifies defect/s & preliminary root causes, explains the rationale
• Proposes solutions on quality/productivity and work on milestones with managers
• Expertise in research – finding specific information (eg: products, regulations etc) in a timely manner.
• Prepares key insight trends and share reports on regular basis.
• Provide feedbacks to the associates and close loop on audit observations.
• Respond to stakeholders with guidance and flags any updates to Lead/Manager

About the team
Amazon is an E-commerce and Cloud Computing company with headquarters in Seattle, Washington. Since 1995, Amazon has focused on being “the world’s most customer centric company.” Our customers are worldwide, and include not just consumers, but also our sellers and vendors (selling partners). World-class retail brands and individual sellers increase their sales and reach new customers by leveraging the power of the Amazon e-commerce platform. To meet our selling partners’ needs, our smart, diverse, customer-obsessed employees are constantly innovating and building on new ideas.
The Operational Risk Compliance (ORC) organization exists to keep our customers and partners safe, protect associates, and ensure legal and regulatory compliance. We coordinate the aspects of product transactions that are regulated (distribution, shipping, sale, and import/export). Global Solutions and Risk Compliance (GSRC) is the operational arm of the ORC organization. This involves analyzing product import documentation and flagging hazardous risks. We are also responsible for keeping Amazon customers safe and informed by coordinating actions around worldwide program teams to classify products and ensure Amazon’s product listings follow regulatory and legal compliance guidelines. These actions include removing products from the site and from our warehouses, and contacting customers with pertinent sustainability information. The ORC team partners with GSRC supports regulatory compliance requirements for Amazon’s worldwide programs such as Dangerous Goods, Chemical Safety Compliance, Global Trade Services, Transport Risk Compliance, Sustainability, Extended Producer Responsibility and Food Safety. GSRC has offices across India, China, Poland, Romania, Jordan, Philippines and Costa Rica and supports compliance related needs for worldwide Amazon marketplaces.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree
- 1+ years of logistics, transportation, supply chain, import/export operations, or data entry/data administration experience
- Knowledge of Excel at a basic level (e.g., UX navigation, math & logical functions, lookup functions, etc.)
- Speak, write, and read fluently in English
- Work 40 hours/week, and overtime as required
- Experience performing accurate data entry and analysis

Preferred qualifications

- High school or equivalent diploma
- Bachelor's degree in logistics, transporation, supply chain, or business
- Licensed customs broker
- Experience in international logistics, cross-border transportation and supply chain, or U.S. Customs rules and regulations
- Experience in customs

title: Mistrz Utrzymania Ruchu (m/k)
descriptionHtml:
Nasz zespół ds. utrzymania ruchu i infrastruktury jest centralnym ogniwem zaangażowania firmy Amazon w innowacyjność. W miarę rozwoju i przystosowania się firmy Amazon do ciągłych zmian, zespół ten dba o to, aby wykorzystywane przez nas narzędzia i technologie również szły z duchem czasu. Mistrz utrzymania ruchu i infrastruktury pomaga nam być zawsze o krok do przodu, wdrażając najnowsze technologie i identyfikując nowe, wydajne sposoby pracy. Zwraca szczególną uwagę na nasze procesy, aby pomóc utrzymać wysokie standardy, a także wprowadza ulepszenia, aby podnieść je jeszcze wyżej.

Key job responsibilities
• Modelowanie najlepszych praktyk w zakresie bezpiecznego użytkowania sprzętu i monitorowanie zespołów w celu zapewnienia, że wszyscy przestrzegają właściwych procesów
• Śledzenie wydajności sprzętu poprzez kontrole wizualne, monitorowanie stanu technicznego i zadania związane z konserwacją zapobiegawczą oraz, w razie potrzeby, planowanie dodatkowych czynności serwisowych
• Nadzorowanie techników na zmianie w celu wspierania ich rozwoju i pełnienie roli pierwszego punktu kontaktu dla inżynierów utrzymania ruchu i infrastruktury
• Rozwiązywanie problemów związanych z urządzeniami w celu ograniczenia przestojów w pracy, umożliwiając jak najszybszą obsługę paczek
• Udział w poszukiwaniu sposobów ciągłego usprawnienia systemów i standaryzacji procesów w całej sieci europejskiej


A day in the life
Dzień z życia
Osoba na tym stanowisku zarządza zespołem na swojej zmianie, upewniając się, że odpowiedni sprzęt jest dla każdego dostępny i że działa prawidłowo. Obejmuje to monitorowanie procesów w celu zapewnienia przestrzegania przepisów i zasad oraz zagwarantowanie, że przeprowadzana jest konserwacja zapobiegawcza w celu zwiększenia niezawodności sprzętu.
Biorąc pod uwagę wszystko, co obserwuje podczas swojej pracy, przedstawia sugestie dotyczące ulepszeń, aby nasze systemy były bardziej wydajne i produktywne, a następnie wdraża je w obrębie całej UE. Monitoruje również procesy za pomocą narzędzi takich jak Scada, aby zagwarantować ich wydajność, a także ściśle współpracuje ze swoim bezpośrednim przełożonym, pomagając w zadaniach administracyjnych.
Osoba na tym stanowisku pracuje w jednym z naszych centrów logistycznych w systemie zmianowym, który obejmuje niektóre weekendy oraz pracę nocną. W miarę rozwoju doświadczenia w tym ekscytującym segmencie firmy Amazon otrzyma dobre przygotowanie do awansu na wyższe stanowiska.




About the team
Dział utrzymania ruchu i infrastruktury pracuje nad zapewnieniem niezawodności urządzeń firmy Amazon. W skład działu wchodzą wyspecjalizowani technicznie, utalentowani inżynierowie pod przewodnictwem doświadczonej kadry kierowniczej. Działają oni wspólnie przy konserwacji, diagnostyce i naprawach urządzeń w globalnej sieci centrów logistycznych. Od instalacji zautomatyzowanych systemów pakowania, przez nadzór nad ogólną konserwacją wyposażenia technicznego w centrach logistycznych, po naprawę kluczowego sprzętu dystrybucyjnego – zespół ten zajmuje się większością aspektów technicznej strony działalności firmy Amazon. Additionally, the OMR will participate in weekly case management review meetings as necessary. Additional Job Elements include:
- Lift up to 49 pounds and frequently push, pull, squat, bend, and reach

- Work in an environment that is subject to variable temperatures and weather (delivery stations include outside loading departments)

For those that do not have an adult First Aid, CPR, AED certification from the American Heart Association or American Red Cross, must obtain within 3 weeks of start date.

descriptionHtml:
Join our dynamic AWS team and become a critical guardian of global cloud infrastructure! You'll play a pivotal role in maintaining the heartbeat of the world's most innovative technology platform, ensuring seamless data center operations that power millions of businesses and services worldwide.

Data Center Technicians should be willing to work both independently and with a team. Work prioritization, organizational skills, effective communication, and the ability to react quickly are critical to success. In addition to hardware and network repair, candidates will install equipment, create documentation, innovate solutions, and fix problems within the data center space. - Serving as a primary contact point for both internal and external stakeholders, including engineers, software developers, vendors, and contractors

Physical requirements:

Candidates must be able to travel (over 50 miles) or commute (less than 50 miles) to active data center sites as required by business needs.

A day in the life
As a Data Center Technician professional, you have industry-leading technical abilities and demonstrate a breadth of knowledge while you:
-Take ownership of technical issues brought by their customer base, engaging other teams when needed to drive resolution
-Solve problems at their root and step back to understand the broader context
-Maintain service level agreements through the implementation of proactive issue detection and reporting

You will be required to work shift work that will include days/nights/weekends/holidays. Traveling within and outside of the regional work area is required. You will be responsible for having a reliable personal vehicle and valid driver's license to travel within the regional work area, as company transportation will not be provided.

- 1+ years of computer/server hardware troubleshooting or related IT experience
- High school or equivalent diploma
- Work a flexible schedule including weekends, nights, and holidays

- Knowledge of network design, protocols and Layer 1/2 troubleshooting
- Associate's degree in a relevant field (e.g., Computer Science, Networking Engineering), or experience in a relevant field (e.g., Computer Science, Networking Engineering)

title: Sr. Systems Development Engineer , Prime Air
descriptionHtml:
Prime Air is seeking a Senior Systems Development Engineer to own the certification requirements and the certification plan for the MK30 unmanned aircraft system. You will author the plan that tells regulators how we intend to show our design is safe, and you will negotiate the means of compliance that make that plan binding. EASA is our first market. The plan you write and the agreements you reach there set the template every market after it inherits.

Your core technical problem is that one aircraft must satisfy many regulators. Each country and region brings its own airworthiness requirements, operational constraints, and expectations for evidence. You will maintain the single authoritative set of certification requirements across those jurisdictions, analyze where authorities diverge, and drive the resulting requirements into the design. Where a national requirement would otherwise force a redesign later, you will find it now and get it into the requirements baseline. The goal is a design that clears today's markets and does not have to be re-architected for the next ones or for the aircraft that follow MK30.

You will work as the engineering counterpart to the Senior Technical Program Manager on this team. The TPM owns the plans, schedules, compliance tracking, and leadership reporting. You own the technical content: what the requirements are, how we comply, what evidence proves it, and what we have committed to the authority. When a regulator questions an approach, you are the engineer who defends it.

Key job responsibilities

- Own the certification requirements baseline across every jurisdiction Prime Air operates in or plans to enter. Maintain it as one requirements set with jurisdiction attribution, not a document per country.
- Perform regulatory delta analysis across authorities (EASA, FAA, CASA, DGCA, CAA, JCAB, and others). Determine where a single design and a single evidence set satisfy multiple authorities, and where they genuinely cannot.
- Drive country- and region-specific requirements into system, software, and hardware requirements early enough to shape the design. Protect MK30 and future designs from late, market-driven rework.
- Lead novel certification approaches for the Prime Air UAS aligned to emerging regulations.
- Author and own the program certification plan. Keep it current as the certification basis, the design, and the authority's expectations evolve, and make it the document a regulator can read to understand our design approach without a briefing.
- Build the evidence reuse argument that carries approvals between authorities, including bilateral validation paths, so each new market is a delta rather than a new program.
- Write the compliance arguments and residual risk positions for open items, deferred defects, and partially satisfied objectives, and defend them directly with authority staff and designees.
- Partner with the regulatory administration team to monitor emerging regulation and rulemaking, assess the design and requirements impact, and fold accepted requirements into the baseline before they block a market entry.
- Build the mechanisms that make this scale: requirements and traceability structures that carry jurisdiction tagging, reusable compliance matrix patterns, and plan templates that a second aircraft program can adopt.

title: Risk Specialist I, EAP
descriptionHtml:
Amazon's Worldwide Environmental Assurance and Protection (EAP) team is responsible for ensuring that Amazon's global operation is the benchmark for environmental excellence across all similar industries. EAP transforms environmental regulatory compliance into a zero-defect process through simple, scalable, and sustainable solutions that protect the business, our communities, and the environment.

The Risk Specialist I drives regulated waste compliance across the 2-4 sites they support. This specialist executes the organization's environmental compliance plans at the site level, tracks waste compliance obligations to closure, and partners with site and operations teams to meet compliance milestones. They conduct site inspections, maintain hazardous waste accumulation and manifesting records, and surface gaps through regular program controls.

The ideal candidate brings working knowledge of regulated waste requirements, including RCRA, DOT, and applicable state hazardous waste rules. They communicate technical compliance requirements clearly to site leaders, operations partners, and legal stakeholders, and use data to find gaps, prioritize fixes, and improve conformance across their sites.

This role requires sound independent judgment, comfort with ambiguity, and the ability to run the right mechanisms and manage competing priorities to meet compliance objectives in a dynamic, high-pace operations environment. If you are motivated by solving regulatory compliance problems in the field, this role is for you.

Key job responsibilities
- Own the execution and delivery of regulated waste compliance projects and activities, including developing standard operating procedures, workflows, and inspection routines, to mitigate identified risks across the sites you support.
- Apply risk management methods such as waste compliance audits and site inspections to monitor compliance thresholds, test controls, and take corrective action when findings arise.
- Collaborate with site teams, compliance operations, and operations partners to understand business needs, clarify waste compliance requirements, and drive productive discussions that build consensus.
- Identify process improvement opportunities and work with process owners to improve conformance, reduce risk, and increase operational efficiency.
- Prepare clear and concise documentation, including status reports, audit results, metrics, and project communications, so the right information reaches the right audience at the right time.
- Travel expected up to 50% of the time.

A day in the life
Your morning might begin by reviewing incoming risk-related requests and prioritizing your project tasks. You will spend time conducting audits or risk assessments, updating documentation, and coordinating with compliance operations and partner teams. Throughout the day, you will track project milestones, resolve roadblocks, and communicate progress to stakeholders. You will also look for ways to streamline existing processes and ensure your risk area stays aligned with current regulations and team objectives.

About the team
Our team is dedicated to protecting Amazon's customers and business by proactively managing risk across a broad range of areas, from regulatory compliance to operational resilience. We work closely with legal, operations, and business partners to deliver practical risk solutions and build a strong culture of compliance. We value collaboration, continuous learning, and creative problem-solving, and we are committed to building an inclusive environment where every team member can grow and make an impact.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) or related field
- 2+ years of experience in environmental compliance, regulated waste management, or workplace risk investigations
- Experience interpreting and applying environmental regulations (RCRA, DOT, and applicable state hazardous waste rules)
- Experience collecting and analyzing data to identify compliance gaps and drive corrective actions

Preferred qualifications

- Experience with Microsoft Office including Outlook, Word, and Excel
- 4+ years of compliance program management, legal, governance, audit, risk/loss prevention, or equivalent experience
- Experience managing a regulated waste program across multiple sites, including hazardous waste accumulation, manifesting, and disposal
- Hazardous waste certification such as RCRA or DOT (49 CFR) training, or 40-hour HAZWOPER

title: Technical Program Manager - Analytics & GenAI, Data Center Procurement Governance (DCPG)
descriptionHtml:
Are you a builder who takes a messy business process and, in days not quarters, turns it into a working data-and-AI solution people actually adopt? Do you pair that with the technical depth to design the solution well, raise the quality bar on what gets shipped, and lift the builders around you?

As Technical Program Manager, Analytics & GenAI within Data Center Procurement Governance (DCPG), you will be a hands-on, technically deep builder-enabler who takes generative-AI and analytics capabilities end to end: from the business process and the build decision, through the solution and the data it stands on, to the enablement and adoption that make it stick. This is a build-and-own role, not a coordinate-and-hand-off role.

You bring a higher technical bar than a typical program manager - strong enough in data and software practice to build fit-for-purpose solutions quickly, review the quality and security of what the team builds, and mentor other builders. You are a program manager first: you own the problem, the build decision, and the outcome and you have the technical depth to deliver it yourself and raise the bar for everyone around you.

This role works across a broad array of procurement practitioners and partner teams in a global, matrixed organization. The ability to make an impact and drive outcomes amid an ambiguous, complex landscape is critical. Due to the global nature of the role, flexibility across time zones is needed.

Your role includes:

- Take a business process, understand it deeply, and iterate quickly to generate solutions - re-engineering the workflow and folding its logic into the build rather than automating it as-is.

- Build generative-AI, analytics, and automation solutions end to end on modern low-code and GenAI platforms - fit-for-purpose, capability-grade solutions you own through iteration, built close to the business process.

- Build and own analytics and insight - dashboards, metrics, and self-updating mechanisms that surface signal proactively to decision-makers.

- Be data-strong: design and stand behind the data foundation your solutions rely on so analytics and GenAI output can be trusted, not just believed.

- Provide technical leadership and mentorship, review the quality and security of what the team builds (including code and application-security review), uphold engineering and data-integrity standards, and grow the capability of the builders around you.

- Partner with specialist engineering teams on heavier, full-stack platform builds - scoping and handing off work that belongs there, while owning rapid, process-proximate building yourself.

- Change management & adoption (owned, not an afterthought), own landing and adoption for what you deliver: enablement, training, feedback loops, and iteration until the solution is the way the work gets done. A build that doesn't land hasn't delivered; you are accountable for adoption outcomes, not just shipped tools.


Key job responsibilities
1. Translate business processes into solutions — owning the 'what to build and why' decision and re-engineering workflows where that delivers more value than automating as-is.
2. Design, build, and iterate GenAI, analytics, and automation solutions end to end, taking them from idea to adopted state.
3. Build analytics, dashboards, and reporting mechanisms that measure outcomes and surface insight proactively.
4. Design and stand behind the data foundation (sources, validation, provenance) that keeps analytics and GenAI trustworthy.
5. Provide technical leadership: review the quality and security of solutions the team ships (including code and application-security review) and mentor other builders.
6. Partner with specialist engineering teams on full-stack/platform builds, scoping clear boundaries and handoffs.
7. Drive change management and adoption to measurable targets across multiple stakeholder groups and regions.
8. Operate independently in ambiguity, building fit-for-purpose with incomplete or evolving requirements.

A day in the life
- No standard day — global scope and much variety: a morning sync with US team members, a working session with APAC, an EMEA call to close.
- Real time spent building — designing a solution, shipping a GenAI tool, or reviewing and uplifting a teammate's build — not only coordinating.
- Your customers are the data center procurement teams and partner teams; stakeholders include legal, finance, assurance, and security colleagues.
- You are both the builder who ships and the technical mentor the team relies on for review and quality.

About the team
Data Center Procurement Governance (DCPG) is a global function that enables Amazon's data center procurement organization to execute at scale — building the operational backbone of programs, mechanisms, systems and tooling, analytics, and generative AI that lets the procurement organization move faster. This role is the analytics and GenAI build-and-enable capability at the center of that work, partnering with procurement to build and iterate, whilst working with specialist engineering teams for heavier platform development and scaling.

Inclusive Team Culture
AWS values curiosity and connection. Our department, Data Center Planning and Delivery (DCPD), sponsors a Women's Leadership Program that supports the growth and development of female builders across the organization. Our employee-led and company-sponsored affinity groups promote inclusion and empower our people to take pride in what makes us unique. Our inclusion events build stronger, more collaborative teams. Our continual innovation draws on the bold ideas, fresh perspectives, and passionate voices our teams bring to everything we do.

Basic qualifications

- 4+ years in technical program management, building or delivering technical solutions hands-on (not only coordinating engineering teams).
- Experience developing and deploying GenAI, analytics, or automation solutions to production and iterating them.
- Strong data capability — designing and working with data models, validation, and the data foundation solutions rely on (e.g. SQL and a general-purpose/scripting language such as Python).
- Working knowledge of technology risk, data/security, and compliance considerations — builds to security and quality standards and shepherds solutions through review.
- Experience driving change management and adoption of technical solutions to measurable outcomes.

Preferred qualifications

- Experience with automation or scripting (Python or equivalent) and building analytics, BI, or dashboards.
- Experience mentoring or raising the technical bar for other builders.
- Track record of designing data validation, guardrails, and lineage into solutions that consume untrusted or migrated data.
- Experience influencing stakeholders across functions, geographies, or business units.
- Domain exposure to procurement, supply chain, or data center supply/delivery.
- Experience architecting or operating solutions on AWS.
- Experience defining outcome metrics (adoption, time saved, quality) and presenting recommendations to leadership.

title: Reliability Maintenance Engineering Technician
descriptionHtml:
The Reliability Maintenance Engineering (RME) team at Amazon is fundamental to our operations – they’re the ones keeping vital machinery running at all times. As an RME Technician, you’ll maintain a wide range of equipment and workspaces while upholding Health and Safety best practices. You'll help to keep your colleagues safe and prevent machine downtime. Our RME Technicians boost the availability and quality of our equipment and work to enhance the operational environment too.

Key job responsibilities
• Proactive and preventative maintenance tasks on a wide range of site equipment
• Carry out reactive repairs and fault diagnosis in a live distribution warehouse
• Use the latest tools to maximise equipment effectiveness
• Uphold all health and safety policies and practices
• Support the development and progression of on-site apprentices
• Work on continuous improvement projects and roll out best practices across a range of EU sites

A day in the life
Our RME Technicians are based on-site, so they can respond quickly to any machinery issues. You’ll carry out a range of planned preventative maintenance to our sites’ equipment to make sure it’s working safely. As an RME Technician, you’ll also respond promptly to breakdowns, investigating, finding, and implementing solutions as quickly as possible. You’ll also make suggestions for long-term improvements.

Working alongside senior colleagues, you’ll undertake day-to-day maintenance tasks and will liaise with contractors if you need external expertise. You’ll work on a range of shifts to make sure our sites are supported around the clock – allowing Amazon to deliver at the speed we’re known for.

About the team
Our Reliability Maintenance Engineering or RME team keep our equipment performing at its best. We're a technically minded team, made up of excellent team players and guided by experienced leaders. We work together to maintain, troubleshoot and repair equipment across our global network of fulfilment centres. Some of our people are leaders, who oversee the team as they work on exciting technology – some of which only exists at Amazon.

From installing automated packaging systems to overseeing the general maintenance of a site to repairing key distribution equipment, our team handles most aspects of Amazon’s technical side. This includes keeping buildings legally compliant, so everyone is safe, and our sites are operating at maximum efficiency. There are lots of opportunities for progression, both within the RME team and more widely across Amazon.

Everything we do focuses on reducing downtime in Amazon’s crucial operations sites, so customers get their orders on time. We often work during early or late hours to carry out maintenance with minimal disruption, including night shifts. If we spot a better way to do something, we have the skills and the opportunity to develop and introduce completely new processes or cutting-edge tech like Amazon Robotics and our Complex Item Sorter.

Basic qualifications

- NVQ Level 3 in Mechanical, Electrical or Mechatronics, or completed a 4-year UK certified apprenticeship
- Work a flexible schedule/shift/work area, including weekends, nights, and/or holidays
- Experience in engineering
- Experience in electrical or mechanical engineering, or experience in facilities management
- Advanced proficiency in the local language verbally and in writing

Preferred qualifications

- Associate's degree in Mechnical or Electrical
- Experience with material handling equipment (MHE) safety standards accordance with original equipment manufacturer (OEM) and safety standards
- Experience with robotic operation and maintenance

title: Onsite Medical Representative
descriptionHtml:
Join Amazon’s mission to become Earth’s safest place to work! At Amazon, we’ve set the ambitious goal to become the benchmark of safety excellence across all industries in which we operate. The Amazon Workplace Health & Safety (WHS) team sets the strategic direction to provide resources, best practices, and safe environments to proactively manage the health and wellbeing of our workforce. To support these goals, Amazon is seeking an experienced and dynamic Onsite Medical Representative (OMR) to join our team. In this position, you will work closely with the WHS Site Manager, WHS Specialist, and occasionally the Injury Prevention Specialist (IPS). This includes attending weekly associate safety committee meetings, greeting all new hires for the site or through daily one-on-one interaction. Additionally, the OMR will participate in weekly case management review meetings as necessary.

As an OMR, you will independently assess and administer first aid as well as offer guidance to Amazon Associates (AAs) on both occupational and non-occupational injuries or illnesses. You should be passionate about learning and advocating health and wellness principles to consistently support AAs on a daily basis. You will refer care to outside medical providers as needed, and learn about OSHA regulations, risk, and analysis.

The OMR will function as a part of the larger team onsite, assisting with all first aid needs and support safety operations as needed.

Responsibilities include but are not limited to:
- Provide first aid support and make referrals to outside medical providers as necessary.
- Minimize the AA risk of injury through awareness, education, and proactive engagement.
- Maintain all records of care provided to AAs.
- Coordinate and maintain the workers’ compensation and return to work programs for AAs with work-related injuries.
- Provide daily activity logs and end of shift reports.
- Engage with AAs and leadership on operations floor to provide coaching regarding observed at-risk work habits.
- Maintain a clean working environment and ensure appropriate medical supply inventory is maintained.
- Participate in training and certification to facilitate first aid, CPR and AED certifications classes.
- Maintain all first aid, CPR, AED credentials.
- Work flexible shifts which could include days, nights, holidays, and/or weekends.
- Assist with random saliva drug testing protocols.
- Maintain effective care delivery in emergencies and assist emergency response at the site.

Additional Job Elements include:
- Lift up to 49 pounds and frequently push, pull, squat, bend, and reach
- Stand/walk for up to 12 hours during shifts
- Work in an environment where the noise level varies
- Work in an environment that is subject to variable temperatures and weather (delivery stations include outside loading departments)
- Continuously climb and descend stairs (applies to sites with stairs)

For those that do not have an adult First Aid, CPR, AED certification from the American Heart Association or American Red Cross, must obtain within 3 weeks of start date.

Basic qualifications

- High school or equivalent diploma
- Current valid Basic Life Support (BLS) certification by an approved emergency cardiac care (ECC) provider; AND must have one of the following:
- Current valid Emergency Medical Technician (EMT) OR Paramedic Certification from the Department of Health OR the National Registry of Emergency Medical Technicians (NREMT); OR
- Current active Athletic Trainer Certification, by either the Board of Certification (BOC) or equivalent State Certification.

Preferred qualifications

- Certified to teach first aid, CPR, and AED training from American Heart Association or American Red Cross
- Proficient in Microsoft Office
- Experience with an industrial wellness program
- Experience managing musculoskeletal disorders, ergonomics, and coaching on body mechanics
- Demonstrated work experience with OSHA regulations and Workers Compensation
- Proficient in digital recordkeeping
- In the last year, six months job experience in the Military as a Combat Medic (U.S. Army), Field Medic (U.S. Army), Healthcare Specialist (U.S. Army), Hospital Corpsman (U.S. Navy), or Aerospace Medical Service Technician (U.S. Air Force)

title: Technical Program Manager, CS Security
descriptionHtml:
Every customer who contacts Amazon trusts us with their data. Customer Service Application Security keeps that promise for one of Amazon's largest businesses. We threat model new designs, test security controls, investigate issues and build automation that makes security the default for every team that ships.

As our Technical Program Manager (TPM), you'll turn security strategy into launched results. You'll own programs end to end, from security assurance on major launches to automation that scales across teams. You'll weigh risk, cost and speed, and see how design choices ripple through architecture and dependencies. Spot a design that's too risky? You'll pull in senior engineers and escalate to leadership early.

You'll keep momentum when priorities shift. You'll partner with security engineers, software development engineers (SDEs) and engineering managers to secure resources, set milestones and define success metrics. You'll own schedule, scope and communication, clear blockers and plan rollouts that keep connected systems running.

You'll shape where we go next through PR/FAQs (press release and frequently asked questions documents), narratives and Operating Plan (OP1/OP2) inputs. You'll protect builders from burnout, mentor others and help hire the people who grow this team. If you love moving between strategy and execution and care about the customers behind the data, let's talk.

Key job responsibilities
- Own security programs end to end, from requirements and threat modeling through implementation, launch, and post-launch support.
- Turn ambiguous security goals into specifications, prioritized milestones and success metrics.
- Partner with security engineers, software development engineers, and engineering managers to secure resources and gain buy-in.
- Own schedule, scope, and communication. Clear blockers and plan rollouts that keep programs running.
- Drive adoption of security automation and guidance across partner teams.
- Manage third-party providers and evaluate emerging tools.
- Run Correction of Error (COE) reviews and fold the lessons into future plans.
- Apply Agile, Lean or Kaizen methods to streamline security work.
- Write PR/FAQs (press release and frequently asked questions documents), narratives and Operating Plan (OP1/OP2) inputs. Mentor others and help hire.

A day in the life
As a TPM, you're the delivery lead on our high-priority programs. Your morning might start by aligning security engineers and partner teams on scope and milestones for a major launch. Next, you flag a risky dependency and pull in a senior engineer before it slips the schedule. Later, you drive a decision that unblocks adoption of new security automation, or draft a narrative that shapes next year's plan. You'll end the day mentoring a teammate or interviewing a candidate. Every day, you're turning security strategy into launched results that protect customer data.

About the team
Customer Service Application Security protects customer data for one of Amazon's largest internal business units. We're reimagining how security integrates with development, building intelligent automation that keeps customers safe while accelerating delivery.

We're a collaborative team of Security Engineers, Technical Program Managers, and SDEs who move fast, value ownership, and invest heavily in each other's growth. We bridge the gap between security and engineering by championing secure coding standards, building tools that reduce friction for developers, and embedding security early through guardrails and paved paths. We stay ahead through continuous research into emerging threats and new techniques and best practices.

Diverse Experiences
Amazon Security values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why Amazon Security?
At Amazon, security is central to maintaining customer trust and delivering delightful customer experiences. Our organization is responsible for creating and maintaining a high bar for security across all of Amazon’s products and services. We offer talented security professionals the chance to accelerate their careers with opportunities to build experience in a wide variety of areas including cloud, devices, retail, entertainment, healthcare, operations, and physical stores.

Inclusive Team Culture
In Amazon Security, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Ongoing DEI events and learning experiences inspire us to continue learning and to embrace our uniqueness. Addressing the toughest security challenges requires that we seek out and celebrate a diversity of ideas, perspectives, and voices.

Training & Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, training, and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why flexible work hours and arrangements are part of our culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve.

Basic qualifications

- 3+ years of technical product or program management experience
- 3+ years of project management disciplines including scope, schedule, budget, quality, along with risk and critical path management experience
- Experience managing programs across cross functional teams, building processes and coordinating release schedules
- Experience in system design

Preferred qualifications

- 3+ years of working directly with engineering teams experience
- Experience developing and executing/delivering product and technical roadmaps
- 2+ years of software development experience
- Bachelor's degree in engineering, computer science or equivalent
- Experience managing cross-functional programs and release schedules

descriptionHtml:

title: Long-term Strategy & Planning, Hub Delivery
descriptionHtml:
The Sr. Strategy and Planning PM will work in a fast-paced, dynamic environment and communicate business conditions and decisions effectively with stakeholders across multiple groups and levels. In this role, a Sr. Strategy and Planning PM will seek out problems, dive deep into data, earn trust of partner teams, and deliver results that can have a large scale influence. This role is a blend of long term strategic planning, that requires quick decision-making, with incomplete data, while also thinking big and influencing the long term direction of the network. The end goal of this role is to answer the question of how we can expand Hub Delivery to our customers in a safer, faster, more efficient, and more cost-effective manner.

Key job responsibilities
At Amazon, we are working to be the most Customer-centric company on earth. A customer experience that we are constantly looking to take to a new level is how we fulfill and deliver customers' orders. We are doing so by building a world class last mile operation capable of exceeding the expectations of our customers by ensuring that their orders are delivered as quickly, accurately, and cost effectively as possible.

The Hub Delivery product allows local small businesses to partner with Amazon to provide flexible and cost-effective delivery service to delight customers globally. This is an emerging Amazon Logistics (AMZL) delivery channel, and is on an exponential growth trajectory globally.

The Sr PM will work in a fast-paced, dynamic environment and communicate business conditions and decisions effectively with stakeholders across multiple groups and levels. In this role, a Sr. PM will seek out problems, dive deep into data, earn trust of partner teams, and deliver results that can have a large scale influence. This role is a blend of long term strategic planning, that requires quick decision-making, with incomplete data, while also thinking big and influencing the long term direction of the network. The end goal of this role is to answer the question of how we can expand Hub Delivery to our customers in a safer, faster, more efficient, and more cost-effective manner.

A day in the life
- Lead long-term network planning and process standardization for the US and Canada.
- Define the best Network Topology solution by leveraging on optimization tool sets to find answers for critical strategic questions such as how many facilities to build, what kinds they should be, where to put them, how to expect them to operate in the larger context of AMZL, and how to connect them in our transportation system.
- Actively work to remove bottlenecks. Create scalable mechanisms and best practices. Use network planning knowledge to influence future tools and features enhancement.
- Communicate and drive long term initiatives. Proactively identify gaps and opportunities. Manage various planning cycles (3YF/OP1/OP2) timelines and deliverables.
- Lead projects for cross-functional teams focused on the delivery of new features and tools service that meet cost optimization and delivery experience maximization goals.
- Proactively identify gaps and opportunities in the process/solution by performing continuous benchmarking with developed countries network.
- Drive clear, precise, and regular communication with stakeholders to include ongoing project/program status via monthly and quarterly planning reviews.
- Up to 10% travel and ability to support international time zones.

Basic qualifications

- 5+ years of program or project management experience
- Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements
- Experience owning program strategy, end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership

Preferred qualifications

- 2+ years of driving process improvements experience
- Master's degree, or MBA in business, operations, human resources, adult education, organizational development, instructional design or related field
- Experience in supply chain

title: Mechatronics & Robotics Tech
descriptionHtml:
About Maintenance at Amazon

Operations is at the heart of Amazon’s business. We are known for our speed, accuracy, and exceptional service. Our buildings deliver tens of thousands of products to hundreds of countries worldwide, every day. Reliability Maintenance & Engineering (RME) are the business partners that work tirelessly behind the scenes to make it all happen. We drive continuous improvement and maintain all of the Robotics and Material Handling Equipment (MHE) to ensure our customers are met with the Amazon smile. Come join us on our journey!

About the Role

As a Mechatronics & Robotics Technician, you will use your skills to support the Operations Maintenance team in repairing and maintaining material handling equipment and pneumatic systems throughout the building. You will have the opportunity to install, maintain, and repair automated packaging and distribution equipment. In addition to developing your skills, you will mentor junior technicians to grow in their roles.

What Do We Offer?

Amazon offers competitive compensation packages including comprehensive healthcare benefits starting on Day 1, matching 401(k) program, and up to 20 weeks of paid parental leave. But wait, there is more: We provide lightweight fire-resistant daily wear and composite toe safety shoes for your safety!

Here is what you can expect with the Reliability & Maintenance Engineering (RME) selection process for Mechatronics & Robotics Technicians: (Timeframe: Approximately 30-days)

Step 1: Congratulations! You successfully submitted your application!

Step 2: Amazon Recruiting will review your application and invite the most qualified candidate to complete a pre-employment assessment.

Step 3: If you meet the role qualifications, you will receive an invitation from Amazon Recruiting (do-not-reply@criteriacorp.com) to begin your Criteria assessment. You have 5 days to complete.

Step 4: Once you successfully meet the pre-employment assessment requirements, you will be invited to complete a video interview. Your video interview invitation will be from HireVue (interviews@hirevue.com) and you will have 7 days to record your interview.

Step 5: Your video interview will be reviewed by the Amazon Hiring Team and you will be notified of next steps via email within 5 business days.


Key job responsibilities
Key job responsibilities include, but are not limited to:
- You will promote a safe working environment by following all safety procedures
- You will complete preventative maintenance routines with proper documentation
- You will troubleshoot electrical and mechanical problems related to all Material Handling Equipment (MHE) which includes belts, motors, photo-eyes, relays, and more
- You will maintain a positive working relationship across all of the Amazon Operations facility
- You must be able to move up to 49lbs, stand and walk during shifts lasting up to 12 hours, climb ladders and gangways safely, and without limitation, as well as perform regular bending, lifting, stretching, and reaching both below the waist and above the head

Please note that while we strive to accommodate employees' preferences for shift assignments, due to operational requirements and scheduling constraints, we cannot guarantee a specific shift assignment.

Basic qualifications

title: Safety Technician
descriptionHtml:
Keeping our people safe and well at work is a top priority at Amazon. Our Safety Technicians play an essential role in making this happen. This role is an opportunity to start your career in workplace safety and develop through a global company. You'll work closely with our experts to monitor your site, which means you'll get to see the difference that you make to people's wellbeing every day.

Key job responsibilities
- Carry out risk assessments and audits.
- Monitor the site to make sure processes are in line with Amazon's safety procedures.
- Create and update reports on safety metrics for colleagues to review.
- Work with colleagues in Operations and across the business on safety-related tasks and offer guidance on processes.
- Support in putting new safety measures in place.

A day in the life
You'll be based at one of our sites. This means that you can closely track what's happening and people can easily ask you any questions throughout their shifts. This role is all about spotting potential issues before they happen. You'll spend a lot of time checking the site and getting to know the way that people use equipment. By understanding how every task and machine works, you'll be able to think about the best way to keep processes safe. You'll also be one of the people to put safety changes into action, which means you'll get to work closely with lots of people. Alongside your daily and weekly tasks, you'll offer support to our Operations team on ad-hoc safety-related work. Safety is so important to Amazon, and you'll help us gather the vital data that keeps us on top of our processes and ahead of any issues. You'll also share that data with people across the business and work with other teams to make sure they're putting safety first.

About the team
The Workplace Health and Safety (WHS) team plays a crucial role in keeping our people mentally and physically well at work. Our team works with managers, associates and local governments across our sites, ensuring compliance with Amazon's policies and legal regulations, and guaranteeing the safety of our work environments. The team offers a variety of opportunities, from Safety Technicians to Programme Managers. Regardless of your role, you'll contribute to the development and implementation of the safety strategy across the entire network.

Basic qualifications

descriptionHtml:

Le responsabilità principali includono l'elaborazione di transazioni HR, la gestione di problematiche relative a orari e presenze e il supporto di base ai dipendenti, con escalation delle questioni complesse a figure di livello superiore. Gli Associate Partner possono supportare più siti all'interno del loro Cluster di riferimento e fungere da punto di contatto principale per le richieste HR di base. In qualità di Associate Partner all'interno del team One PXT, supporterai la realizzazione di una employee experience eccellente in ogni interazione. Questo ruolo richiede una presenza accogliente, garantendo al contempo un supporto accurato e tempestivo su temi legati a benefit, policy e payroll. È previsto che tu lavori in presenza presso un sito operativo Amazon.

The applicable collective agreement for this role is CCNL per i dipendenti del settore Logistica, Trasporto Merci e Spedizione. The position is classified at level 3 or above, depending on the candidate's skills, competences and experience.

Key job responsibilities
- Fornire supporto reattivo, cordiale e professionale ai dipendenti attraverso diversi canali (di persona, via email, telefono), offrendo informazioni accurate e tempestive su benefit, policy, payroll e altri argomenti HR.

- Contribuire a una cultura aziendale positiva e inclusiva, supportando e implementando iniziative di employee engagement e riconoscimento,

- Collaborare con i responsabili e i team di supporto per promuovere e formare i dipendenti sull'utilizzo degli strumenti self-service — sia basati sull'intelligenza artificiale che tradizionali — e delle risorse HR, migliorando l'employee experience complessiva e l'efficienza operativa. title: Program Planning & Scheduling Analyst, ALG Scheduling & Risk Mgmt
descriptionHtml:
Are you ready to get in on the ground floor of Amazon’s long-term initiative to design, launch and maintain a constellation of Low Earth Orbit satellites to provide low-latency, high-speed broadband connectivity to unserved and underserved communities around the world?

It’s Day 1 for Amazon’s next billion-dollar business and the Amazon Leo for Government business is looking for an entrepreneurial minded Program Planning & Scheduling Analyst to work in a start-up environment who is passionate about technology, who thinks/acts globally, and has the ability to create and implement solutions, processes and controls with a focus on the public sector.

The ALG team is focused on Government customers around the world, including U.S. DoD and other national security customers.

The successful candidate will be responsible for executing day-to-day program planning & scheduling tasks within ALG, providing qualitative and quantitative data analysis for program performance management, ensuring the business meets critical deliverables, program schedules (Integrated Master Schedule), as well as risk and opportunity tracking, management, and mitigation.

This leader will work cross-functionally alongside the program finance team, as well as the program management and engineering teams to ensure Government-funded programs are tracked and performed on cost and schedule.

While still in the start-up phase, ALG will be tracking performance metrics from an internal management perspective for program performance.

The program planning organization will have responsibility for aligning our product roadmaps with ALG availability, ensuring we have products Government customers can use when Amazon Leo service comes online.

title: Senior Technical Program Manager, CloudTune
descriptionHtml:
The CloudTune Capacity Management and Planning (CaMP) team is responsible for strategically planning, procuring, optimizing, and managing the cloud compute infrastructure that powers Amazon's global retail products and services. Our mission is to ensure Amazon has the right compute capacity, at the right time and cost, while maximizing infrastructure utilization and minimizing waste. We support year-round business operations and major global traffic events, including Prime Day, Q4 holidays, the Super Bowl, and Prime Video original launches.

We are seeking a highly analytical and technically strong Senior Technical Program Manager to lead complex, cross-organizational infrastructure optimization and capacity planning initiatives. This role will own the strategy, roadmap, and execution of programs that improve compute efficiency, optimize infrastructure investments, and enable Amazon to scale reliably and cost-effectively.

The ideal candidate combines deep technical understanding of cloud infrastructure with strong business judgment, analytical rigor, and the ability to influence decisions across engineering, finance, economics, and AWS leadership. This is a high-impact role requiring the ability to navigate ambiguity, challenge existing mechanisms, and translate complex infrastructure constraints into scalable, automated solutions.

- Develop and execute a comprehensive capacity optimization strategy spanning idle capacity forecasting, resource reuse, Sweep, Reserved Instance expiration, resizing, and infrastructure returns.

- Establish leading indicators, forecasting mechanisms, and automated controls to proactively manage IMR performance and identify corrective actions before financial thresholds are breached.

- Partner with engineering, AWS, finance, and business stakeholders to drive systemic efficiency improvements, influence investment priorities, and deliver sustainable reductions in infrastructure waste.

- Own executive-level reporting on IMR performance, cost drivers, risks, and mitigation plans, ensuring clear accountability for achieving organizational efficiency goals.

title: Mechanical Engineer, Electronics Packaging, Avionics Mechanical
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Leo is Amazon's low Earth orbit satellite network. Our mission is to deliver fast, reliable internet connectivity to customers beyond the reach of existing networks. From individual households to schools, hospitals, businesses, and government agencies, Amazon Leo will serve people and organizations operating in locations without reliable connectivity.

Achieving that mission requires engineers who thrive on solving complex, multidisciplinary problems and delivering hardware that performs flawlessly from manufacturing through launch and years of operation in space.

As a Mechanical Engineer on the Avionics Mechanical team, you will design and develop the mechanical implementation of spacecraft electrical systems from early architecture through flight hardware. You will work alongside Mechanical, Electrical, Thermal, Reliability, and Manufacturing engineers to develop innovative solutions that protect sensitive electronics while enabling efficient assembly, qualification, production, and long-term mission success.

This role requires strong mechanical engineering fundamentals, sound problem-solving skills, and the ability to work across disciplines to develop reliable flight hardware. You will own hardware throughout the product lifecycle while balancing performance, reliability, manufacturability, cost, and schedule.

Export Control Requirement: Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

Key job responsibilities
- Design and develop spacecraft avionics hardware from concept through production.
- Partner with Electrical Engineering to integrate circuit boards, connectors, harnesses, and electronic assemblies into robust mechanical designs.
- Perform engineering analyses and trade studies to support design decisions.
- Develop hardware that withstands launch, vibration, thermal cycling, radiation, and the space environment.
- Support qualification testing, manufacturing, and hardware troubleshooting.
- Collaborate with cross-functional engineering teams to identify and retire technical risk.
- Investigate failures and implement design improvements throughout the product lifecycle.
- Contribute to engineering best practices and continuous improvement efforts.

A day in the life
As a Mechanical Engineer, you'll work closely with engineers across multiple disciplines to develop flight-ready spacecraft hardware. Your day may include designing new avionics hardware, supporting design reviews, analyzing qualification test results, working with manufacturing to resolve hardware issues, or collaborating with suppliers to improve component designs. You'll gain exposure to the full hardware development lifecycle while contributing to products that will operate in one of the most demanding engineering environments.

About the team
The Avionics Mechanical team partners closely with Electrical Engineering to ensure every spacecraft electrical subsystem is mechanically robust throughout manufacturing, launch, and mission life. The team is responsible for the structural implementation of avionics hardware, including enclosure design, packaging architecture, mounting strategies, and environmental protection.

Working alongside Electrical Engineering, Structures, Thermal Engineering, Reliability Engineering, and Manufacturing Engineering, the team develops solutions that protect sensitive electronics from launch loads, vibration, thermal cycling, radiation, and the space environment. Engineers solve challenging problems involving PCB support, connector retention, thermal interfaces, fastener design, electronics packaging, and long-term material durability while balancing system performance with manufacturability.

Beyond flight hardware, the team also develops the specialized qualification hardware, manufacturing fixtures, inspection tooling, and test equipment that enable efficient verification throughout the product lifecycle. We are a highly collaborative organization that values first-principles engineering, technical curiosity, and a bias toward delivering practical solutions that enable reliable spacecraft at scale.

Basic qualifications

- Experience collaborating with cross-functional teams
- 2+ years of working in mechanical engineering or equivalent experience
- Experience with CAD tools and engineering documentation.
- Understanding of mechanical design fundamentals, materials, manufacturing processes, and tolerance analysis.
- Strong problem-solving and communication skills.

Preferred qualifications

- Experience participating in or leading technical collaborations and creating alignment across diverse groups (e.g., hardware engineering, software engineering, program management)
- Experience developing aerospace, defense, medical device, automotive, semiconductor, or consumer electronics products.
- Experience designing electronics packaging or electromechanical assemblies.
- Experience supporting environmental qualification or reliability testing.
- Familiarity with FMEA, DFM/DFA, V&V, and root cause analysis.

title: Data Centre Support Engineer Apprentice - London and Surrounding Areas (18-months Fixed Term Contract)
descriptionHtml:
Are you curious about how the cloud works and eager to play a hands-on role keeping it running? If so, we have an exciting opportunity for you to join our Amazon Web Services (AWS) Infrastructure Services team as a Data Centre Operations (DCO) Apprentice, helping deliver the technology that powers businesses, entertainment, and innovation worldwide.

What is a data centre? A data centre is a specialised facility filled with thousands of computers, servers, and networking equipment that store and process vast amounts of data - powering the services we all rely on, from streaming to online shopping. Our DCO team designs, installs, and maintains the cloud computing infrastructure that keeps AWS running reliably for millions of customers around the world.

About AWS AWS offers an exciting, dynamic environment that encourages creativity while keeping our cloud infrastructure secure, scalable, and cost-effective. The AWS Infrastructure Services team looks after our global data centres - managing the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that keep customers connected to the services they rely on every day.

Throughout your apprenticeship you'll grow both the technical expertise and the practical judgement to keep critical systems running - learning to diagnose and resolve issues, work safely with hardware, and contribute to the reliability of infrastructure that serves customers worldwide. You'll build these skills working alongside experienced technicians, and you'll be at the forefront of the AI infrastructure powering Amazon's most advanced technologies.

A day in the life can involve:

- Supporting the diagnosis and resolution of technical issues across servers, networks, and power systems
- Responding to and prioritising trouble tickets to keep data centre operations running smoothly
- Installing and setting up server racks, following company procedures and safety standards
- Learning to replace hardware components safely and accurately, under guidance from experienced technicians
- Monitoring system performance and contributing to preventative maintenance activities
- Gaining exposure to cyber security principles and system protection best practices
- Collaborating with facilities teams during power and cooling maintenance events
- Participating in small to mid-scale projects that enhance system reliability and efficiency

We welcome individuals from all backgrounds with a keen interest in technology, strong problem-solving skills, and a customer-first mindset. A proactive, organised approach and the ability to communicate technical information clearly matter most. We move fast, fail fast, and fix faster, so you'll be encouraged to learn by doing from day one.

These roles are based in data centres in surrounding areas of London, with specific site details shared later in the recruitment process.

Here at Amazon, it's in our nature to learn and be curious. Within this apprenticeship you'll put newfound knowledge into practice every day, supported by first-class coaching, tailored development, and rewarding work that will empower you to reach new heights and build the future you envision.

You'll gain a vast range of experiences and skills while working towards the Information Communications Technician – Support Technician Professional Level 3 Apprenticeship qualification.
