title: Future Operations Leader - Degree Apprenticeship London (37-month fixed term contract)
descriptionHtml:
Are you ready to step into a leadership role in one of the world's most fast-paced, customer-obsessed operations? This is your opportunity to earn a fully funded degree from a Russell Group university while leading in the heart of Amazon's operations - from day one.

Amazon is looking for ambitious, driven individuals to join our Future Operations Leader Degree Apprenticeship. You'll earn a fully funded BSc (Hons) in Leadership and Project Management while working on the ground in one of our fulfilment centres or operational sites, solving real business challenges alongside experienced leaders. This is a hands-on role, not a desk job - our sites are vast (some the size of several football pitches), and you'll be out across the floor where the action happens, covering real distance as you lead teams, drive change, and make a tangible impact.

At its core, this is a people role. Yes, you'll work with data, processes, and technology - but the heart of operations leadership is people. You'll learn how to motivate a team at 3am, how to have difficult conversations with empathy, how to recognise when someone's struggling, and how to create an environment where people want to do their best work. If you're energised by working with others and want to build your career around leading teams, this programme will give you the foundation to do exactly that.

This role involves shift work, including days, nights, and weekends, because our operations run around the clock and great leaders need to understand every part of that rhythm. You'll rotate through different shift patterns, which means early starts, late finishes, and yes, night shifts. It's a demanding, fast-paced environment with a lot to juggle – you'll need to prioritise quickly, stay composed under pressure, and keep the most important things moving. It's a real step up, and we're looking for people who expect that challenge and are ready to run with it. It's a physical, on-your-feet role - you'll be out on the floor, not behind a desk. It's not for everyone, but if you thrive where no two days feel the same and you want to understand operations from the ground up, it's one of the most valuable parts of the experience.

A day in the life can involve:

- Starting with a team stand-up or shift handover, reviewing priorities, performance metrics, and issues from the previous shift

- Shadowing or supporting a team leader or manager on the floor, getting stuck into real-time problem solving - clearing a bottleneck, supporting a team member, or managing workflow across the site

- Working on a project linked to your degree - building a business case for a process improvement, mapping stakeholders for a site change, or analysing quality and risk data to present back to leadership

- On university weeks, attending masterclasses or webinars and completing coursework, then bringing what you've learned straight back onto the floor

As you progress, you'll build relationships across the site, develop your own leadership style, and take on increasing responsibility.

This could be for you if you're the person who captained a sports team, coached younger students, led a group project, completed your Duke of Edinburgh, volunteered in your community, organised something no one asked you to, or put your hand up to be a prefect. Or maybe you've spent a few years in the workplace and found yourself naturally stepping up - training new starters, leading a team, improving a process, or taking ownership of something bigger than your job description. Leadership isn't about a job title; it's about what you do when no one's told you to. If that sounds like you, this programme is your next step.

Over 37 months, you'll develop the knowledge and skills to lead in a complex operational environment, including:

- Business strategy and how organisations operate

- Project planning, scheduling, budgeting, and delivery within time, cost, and quality constraints

- Leading and managing diverse teams, building trust, and driving performance

- Financial controls, business case development, and performance reporting

- Stakeholder engagement, communication, and influencing at all levels

- Organisational change management - preparing teams and operations for change

- Risk identification, quality assurance, and continuous improvement

- Commercial awareness, procurement, and contract management

- Digital innovation, data-driven technologies, and AI in a business context

What you'll achieve:

- BSc (Hons) Leadership and Project Management

- Level 6 Project Manager Degree Apprenticeship

- CMI Level 5 Certificate in Project Management (dual accredited)

- International Project Management Association (IPMA) Level D qualification

Four qualifications. Fully funded. All earned while working.

This is a blended learning programme. Each module follows a 14-week cycle combining pre-reading and preparation, in-person masterclasses at the university, online learning and webinars, and individual study and assignment writing. You'll be supported throughout by a dedicated Academic Mentor, with progress reviews every 12 weeks involving your Line Manager, plus full access to university resources including library services, wellbeing support, and student societies.

Basic qualifications

- To qualify for this programme, you must:
- Be 18 years or over before the start date (September 2027)
- Have the right to live and work in England at the point of enrolment (June 2027). If you are on a visa, this must enable you to legally work and reside in England for the entire duration of the programme from enrolment.
- Have lived in the UK or in the European Economic Area (EEA) for the last 3 years prior to the start date
- Not be registered to study on a UK government funded course ending August 2027 or later
- Be prepared to travel for external/mandatory training as part of the apprenticeship
- Hold 5 GCSEs at grade 4-9 (A-C) or above (or equivalent) including Maths and English and 3 A Levels at minimum grades ABB (or equivalent). Contextual offers will also apply. https://www.ucas.com/applying/applying-university/individual-needs/contextual-admissions
- Please note, if you have received educational qualifications outside of the UK then we will require a Statement of Comparability to confirm your eligibility for the scheme. Please ensure you obtain one during the application process, through UK ENIC: https://www.enic.org.uk/
- Previous qualifications will be reviewed for funding eligibility and offers are subject to funding approval
- PLEASE NOTE: This position is a 37 month fixed-term contract. You must NOT already have a qualification in a similar subject at the same or higher level than this apprenticeship.
- This Apprenticeship assumes the candidate has some or little knowledge/experience of the occupation

Preferred qualifications

- An interest in operations, logistics, or supply chain environments
- A genuine enthusiasm for leading, motivating, and working with people
- Natural leadership instincts - the kind of person who steps up without being asked
- Resilient and able to prioritise under pressure - staying composed when the pace is demanding and there’s a lot to juggle
- Great communication skills and naturally able to influence others
- A problem-solving mindset and a willingness to learn
- Comfortable with change and able to stay calm in a fast-paced environment
- Happy working in fast-paced warehouse environment, including shift work (days, nights, and weekends)

descriptionHtml:
We're seeking exceptional talent to help develop the next generation of advanced robotics systems that will transform automation at Amazon's scale. We're building revolutionary robotic systems that combine innovative AI, sophisticated control systems, and advanced mechanical design to create adaptable automation solutions capable of working safely alongside humans in dynamic environments. This is a unique opportunity to shape the future of robotics and automation at an unprecedented scale, working with world-class teams pushing the boundaries of what's possible in robotic manipulation, locomotion, and human-robot interaction.

title: Sr. TPM - Sustainability, Technical Standards - WWGS
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for an innovative leader to join Amazon's WWGS retail and industrial development team who is passionate about reducing the environmental impact of the buildings that serve our customers. The ideal candidate will have a strong knowledge of sustainable building practices, carbon accounting, and their application in retail and grocery industrial environments. This position will be responsible for defining sustainable buildings strategy, embedding the Sustainable Building Standard (SBS) into design standards, and leading retrofits and pilots that reduce carbon and water use. You will also own carbon tracking and reporting, from abatement calculations to embodied carbon and bi-annual forecasts.

This position will be part of an exciting, fast-moving business unit, where everyone on the team needs to be entrepreneurial, wear many hats and work effectively in a highly collaborative environment. You will drive initiatives through design, construction, critical infrastructure and operations teams, and translate Worldwide Sustainability goals into WWGS strategy. You are the right person for this job if you prioritize real decarbonization over offsets and have a passion for producing high-quality, data-driven work. You must take ownership of your work, display a great deal of initiative, possess common sense, sound judgment, and a sense of humor.

Key job responsibilities
- Define and drive the sustainable buildings strategy for WWGS. Put decarbonization ahead of offsets, in line with the Climate Pledge.
- Build the Sustainable Building Standard (SBS) into design standards, specifications and reference documents for every building type and project stage. Track and report SBS compliance for new sites, both at design and at construction complete.
- Lead strategy for sustainable retrofit projects and high-value pilots that cut carbon emissions and water use. Pilots should be pay for themselves through positive lifecycle value.
- Do the carbon emissions and abatement calculations, the yearly carbon modeling of each building type, and the building carbon forecasts twice a year. Track embodied carbon for construction materials in EC3.
- Back up sustainability claims for Amazon's annual sustainability reporting. Analyze project and material data to make sure it is accurate and complete.
- Build partnerships with Design, Construction, Critical Infrastructure, Procurement and Operations teams. Use those partnerships to build sustainability into their processes and tools, and to coordinate data collection, such as Bills of Materials.
- Turn Worldwide Sustainability (WWS) guidance and mandates into WWGS plans and initiatives. Respond to pan-Amazon and S-team requests about sustainable buildings.
- Manage workstreams and track progress on carbon, water and SBS goals. Report status, blockers and help needed through monthly and quarterly business reviews.

Basic qualifications

- Minimum 7 years of experience working in sustainability reporting, sustainability assurance, sustainability compliance or legal fields.
- Minimum 5 years of experience in project management and stakeholder engagement, with the proven track record to build stakeholder engagement plans, set clear expectations, and engage cross-functional partners to drive timely, high-quality outcomes.
- Proven track record of analyzing and synthesizing large volumes of qualitative and quantitative data to produce external reports or disclosures in alignment with specific reporting criteria.
- Experience in performing human rights impact assessments or value chain mapping across a large multinational organization to inform sustainability disclosures.
- Deep understanding of the sustainability regulatory landscape.

Preferred qualifications

- Sustainability reporting accreditation/certification (e.g. GRI Certified Sustainability Professional, ISSB (IFRS) Sustainability Fundamentals Certificate).
- Experience directly performing independent third-party assurance or managing external audit firms.
- Experience designing and implementing data collection processes across complex global supply chains involving multiple tiers of suppliers and diverse operational contexts.
- Proficiency in data analysis and visualization tools (e.g., Excel, Tableau, Power BI) to synthesize and present sustainability performance data to diverse audiences.

title: Engineering Operation Technician
descriptionHtml:
Join our dynamic team and become a critical guardian of technological infrastructure! As a Data Center Engineering Technician, you'll play a pivotal role in maintaining the heartbeat of mission-critical technology infrastructure, ensuring seamless operations that power global digital experiences. Your expertise will directly contribute to maintaining an extraordinary 99.999% uptime, keeping the digital world running smoothly and efficiently.

Engineering Technicians are Amazon’s front line when it comes to hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment troubleshooting. They will maintain, operate, and troubleshoot, Data Center Operation’s Mission Critical Facilities, which includes stand-by diesel generators and related fuel systems, as well as three phase electrical systems such as: switch gear, UPSs, PDUs, wet cell batteries and associated systems, CRAC, centrifugal chillers, cooling towers/water chemical system, air handlers and associated systems, pumps, & motors.

We are seeking experienced Engineering Operations Technicians to join our data center operations team, specifically focusing on liquid cooling infrastructure and water distribution systems. This role is vital in maintaining the continuous operation of our advanced cooling systems that support critical data center operations.

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

NOTE: Amazon does not sponsor for immigration, including for H-1B, TN, and other non-immigrant visas, for this role.

NOTE: Lump sum stipend will be provided to eligible candidates who relocate for this position.


Key job responsibilities

• Perform maintenance, troubleshooting, root cause analysis, and repair of liquid cooling systems
• Technical writing to support change management program
• Monitor daily work requests and manage to resolution, and execute projects from conception to completion
• On-site support of contractors, sub-contractors and vendors, ensuring that all work performed is in accordance with established practices, procedures & local legislation

• Regularly lift and/or move up to 39 pounds independently

• Work in an environment requiring provided ear protection

This role supports data centers in various operational stages. The position may be assigned to a facility still under development, which could require travel to established locations for training until your designated site becomes fully operational.

Essential Requirements:
• Ability to travel to or commute between data center locations as needed

Candidates must be able to travel (over 50 miles) or commute (less than 50 miles) to active data center sites as required by business needs.

This role acts as Amazon’s front line when it comes to hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment preventative maintenance (PM) and troubleshooting, reporting to a site’s Data Center Facility Manager (FM). Mechanical equipment includes CRAHU units, centrifugal chillers, cooling towers, water systems, air handlers and associated systems, pumps, and motors. Additional support equipment is included in the scope of the role which includes fire/life safety equipment, building automation systems, and general facilities equipment.

title: Safety Risk Engineer, WHS Design & Engineering
descriptionHtml:
At Amazon, safety is our top priority. We are looking for a WHS Risk Engineer to own machinery safety across multiple sites. In this role you will lead machinery safety inspections and risk assessments, apply the EU Machinery Directive and harmonised standards, and influence engineering and operations leaders to build safe-by-design into our equipment and processes. You'll turn machinery-safety findings into consistent standards that protect our people across the network.

Key job responsibilities
- Lead machinery safety inspections and risk assessments across multiple sites.
- Apply and interpret the EU Machinery Directive (2006/42/EC) and associated harmonised standards.
- Identify machinery and MHE risks and drive the implementation of effective control measures.
- Engage and influence functional leaders to build buy-in to Health & Safety standards and change.
- Use data and metrics to identify gaps and drive improvements across sites.

A day in the life
You work across several sites, moving between machinery inspections, risk assessments and working sessions with engineering and operations leaders.

You dig into how equipment and MHE is designed, installed and used, spot risks that others miss, and drive agreement on the control measures needed.

You use data to see patterns across sites and to prioritise where safety effort has the biggest impact.

A large part of your day is influencing - helping functional leaders understand machinery risk and building buy-in to the Health & Safety standards and changes you recommend.

About the team
The Workplace Health and Safety (WHS) team plays a crucial role in keeping our people mentally and physically well at work. Our team works with managers, associates and local governments across our sites, ensuring compliance with Amazon's policies and legal regulations, and guaranteeing the safety of our work environments. The team offers a variety of opportunities, from Safety Technicians to Programme Managers. Regardless of your role, you'll contribute to the development and implementation of the safety strategy across the entire network.

Basic qualifications

- A Bachelor's degree in electrical, mechanical, civil or industrial engineering or equivalent level of qualification in-line with the European Qualifications Framework (EQF).
- Practical understanding and application of WHS risk assessment and safety standards.
- Relevant experience applying the EU Machinery Directive (2006/42/EC) and associated harmonised standards.
- Experience using data and metrics to identify gaps and drive improvements.
- Experience in English language communication skills, both written and verbal.
- Relevant experience influencing functional leaders and building buy-in to Health & Safety standards and change.

Preferred qualifications

- Preferred qualifications are not required to apply for a position at Amazon. If you have all the basic qualifications above, we'd love to hear from you.
- Experience with Lean, 5S or Kaizen methodologies and continuous improvement.
- Experience using data and metrics to identify gaps and drive improvements.

title: Sr. Sports Research Manager, Prime Video Sports — Live Sports Strategy & Research
descriptionHtml:
Prime Video is redefining how the world watches live sports, delivering NFL Thursday Night Football, NBA, NASCAR, MLB, and global soccer to tens of millions of fans. We seek a Sr. Sports Research Manager to own sports audience measurement for Prime Video Sports, serving as the definitive internal authority on how our live events perform in Nielsen and across the broader measurement landscape.
You will own the Nielsen relationship and end-to-end measurement of every Prime Video Live Sports telecast, authoring audience summaries, reconciling first-party streaming signals against third-party currency, and translating a fast-moving measurement environment into clear business guidance. The ideal candidate pairs deep Nielsen expertise with the judgment to explain why audiences move and the communication skill to make complex concepts land with senior leaders, league partners, and cross-functional stakeholders.


Key job responsibilities
-Own authoritative audience summaries for all Prime Video Sports properties, reporting P2+ AMA on Nielsen Big Data+Panel and Panel-Only bases, including demographics, reach, and minute-by-minute trends. Produce weekly, event-level, and season-to-date reporting on deadline.
-Benchmark Prime Video against the competitive set on a like-for-like basis and manage Nielsen schedule inputs so every telecast is measured accurately and on time.
Reconcile Prime Video first-party device/AMA signals against Nielsen projections and final actuals; build a holistic cross-platform view of linear plus streaming performance.
-Serve as the internal authority on Nielsen methodology; write POVs on currency changes, separate methodology shifts from real audience movement, and represent Prime Video
-Translate measurement into decisions for programming, marketing, PR, finance, and ad sales. Field league and partner data requests, owning accuracy and turnaround.
-Automate recurring reporting and apply AI tools to speed analysis, drafting, and quality-checking, building validation into every workflow so numbers reaching leadership are right the first time.

Basic Qualifications
• 7+ years of media research experience at a network, agency, streamer, league, or research supplier, with end-to-end ownership of measurement deliverables.
• Deep, hands-on expertise with Nielsen national TV measurement (Big Data+Panel, Panel-Only, NNTV, National TV Toolbox, NPOWER-family, NCL schedule input).
• Command of core media math: AMA, rating, share, reach, GRPs, and time-shift windows (live, same-day, VOSDAL, delayed).
• Experience with cross-platform measurement spanning linear TV and streaming, including first-party/impression-based signal integration with third-party currency.
• Advanced Excel and clear, persuasive data storytelling in PowerPoint for senior audiences. Excellent written and verbal communication.
• Bachelor's degree in statistics, economics, communications, marketing, a quantitative social science, or a related discipline. Avid sports fan.

Preferred Qualifications

• Working knowledge of 2025-2026 Nielsen methodology changes (out-of-home expansion, Big Data+Panel transition, co-viewing) and ability to recalibrate benchmarks across breaks.

title: Operations Manager
descriptionHtml:
Der operative Geschäftsbereich ist das Herz von Amazon. Dieser wesentliche Teil unseres Unternehmens sorgt dafür, dass wir Bestellungen effizient erfüllen und versenden, damit unsere Kund:innen ihre Artikel rechtzeitig erhalten. Getragen wird er von Operations Manager:innen, die das Team zusammenführen, um an allen unseren Standorten hervorragende Sicherheit, Qualität und Produktivität zu fördern. Du koordinierst an Deinem Standort andere Manager:innen und erstellst den Betriebsplan, der Deinen Teams bei der Erfüllung ihrer Ziele hilft. Diese Rolle ist voll darauf ausgerichtet, die Operational Excellence zu unterstützen, um das Amazon von Morgen zu schaffen.

Key job responsibilities
- Leitung und Entwicklung eines Teams von Area Manager:innen
- Schichtleitung von Betriebsteams, Handhabung von Problemen und Förderung der Standortleistung
- Analyse der Schichten laut Unternehmensvorgaben und Umsetzung von Maßnahmen zur Verbesserung unserer Operational Excellence
- Enge Zusammenarbeit mit anderen Support-Teams, einschließlich derer für die Bereiche HR, Finanzen, Arbeitsschutz und Sicherheit
- Gestaltung und Umsetzung von Initiativen an allen Standorten zur Verbesserung der Betriebsleistung

A day in the life
Du übernimmst die Schichtleitung an einem unserer Betriebsstandorte. Außerdem fungierst Du als Hauptschnittstelle zwischen mehreren verschiedenen Teams, u. a. den Finanz-, Sicherheits- und Betriebsintegrationsteams. Das bedeutet, dass Du die täglichen Betriebsabläufe an Deinem Standort unmittelbar beobachtest und gleichzeitig auch zu neuen Innovationsmöglichkeiten beiträgst. Ein typischer Arbeitstag umfasst Treffen mit verschiedenen Geschäftsbereichen, eingehende Untersuchungen der Leistungs- und Risikokennzahlen für Standorte sowie Prognosen zur Vorbereitung auf unterschiedliche Nachfragevolumen. Weiterhin bietest Du Deinem Team täglich Mentoring und Coaching. Als Führungskraft unterstützt Du Deine Teammitglieder dabei, ihr Managementpotenzial voll zu entfalten.

About the team
Amazon Logistik (AMZL) ist für die Auslieferung von Millionen von Produkten unserer Kunden und Kundinnen direkt an die Haustür verantwortlich. Die „Last-Mile-Logistik" liefert unsere Pakete in Partnerschaft mit Drittanbietern und realisiert zahlreiche Initiativen zur kontinuierlichen Verbesserung, um Millionen von Kunden zufrieden zu stellen.

Unser Ziel ist es, das Liefererlebnis für unsere Kund:innen so reibungslos wie möglich zu machen und globale Lieferlösungen für unsere neuesten Angebote einzuführen, darunter Amazon Fresh, Prime Now und Amazon Restaurants.

Unsere Arbeit lässt sich in zwei Sparten unterteilen. „Under the Roof" betrifft alles was innerhalb unserer Logistikstandorte passiert und „On the Road" alles was in den Liefergebieten auf der Straße stattfindet. Unsere Mitarbeitenden bereiten die Pakete in entsprechenden Schichten (Nacht, Früh, Spät) auf den täglichen Versand an unsere Lieferteams vor und kümmern sich um Retouren, die nicht ausgeliefert werden konnten.

Jedes Jahr setzen wir neue Maßstäbe in puncto Kundenerlebnis und bieten neue, innovative Lieferdienste an. Wir suchen nach neuen Möglichkeiten, um branchenweite Logistikherausforderungen zu überwinden, sowie nach neuen Ideen, um unseren CO2-Fußabdruck zu reduzieren. Ein Fuhrpark innovativer Fahrzeuge (einschließlich E-Fahrzeugen) und modernste Technologie unterstützen uns dabei.

title: Senior Site EHS Manager
descriptionHtml:
At Amazon, we prioritize health, safety, and well-being above all else. There is nothing more important. To support this priority, Amazon is seeking an experienced and innovative Senior Site Workplace Health and Safety (WHS) Manager to join our team. In this position, you will be responsible for partnering with the site level operations team for your designated site in order to execute company WHS policies and ensure compliance to all applicable local and regional regulations. By leveraging lean principles and Kaizen events, you will lead continuous improvement initiatives to reduce conditional and ergonomic risk in Amazon’s processes to ensure a safe and healthful working environment for our associates.

In this role, you must demonstrate the ability to build trust and confidence with the cross functional operations teams, and influence change through providing comprehensive risk assessments and safety data analysis. To do so, you must be an effective communicator and send clear, concise and consistent messages, both verbally and in writing. You will also be required to instruct and train operations leadership and site WHS professionals in company EHS policies while assisting the regional teams in incorporating our safety standards at their sites. Your experience working in safety programs and your relevant safety, environmental and ergonomic knowledge in an operations environment will be crucial. You will be responsible for developing a team of safety managers and safety professionals at your designated site. Your teams’ success will depend on your ability to create and execute leadership development plans for your larger team. You must demonstrate your ability to clearly communicate organizational direction through your team. As a senior leader in the WHS organization, you will also be responsible for judging and assessing safety talent to select appropriate bench strength for current and future business needs.

Responsibilities include but are not limited to:
- Act as SME of local/regional regulations and company WHS policy.
- Provide guidance and oversight to ensure compliance to all applicable Amazon Safety Policies.
- Measure site performance against published requirements in safety policies. For all deficiencies, identify a plan for the site to implement and fix all identified deficiencies.
- Ensure safety record keeping and data integrity and provides Operations with accurate reporting and metrics to support business safety initiatives.
- Deliver on-time and quality projects to Operations.
- Deep Dive safety metrics and review incident weekly and monthly incident trends to discover trends to justify the allocation of appropriate resources to areas where the safety risk is highest.
- Deep Dive trends and propose action plans to Sr. Leadership on site.
- Audit record keeping practices and Global Safety Database entries to ensure compliance to global safety standards and local regulations.
- Audit the workplace organization and Associate behaviors to ensure that training, auditing and scoring methods are accurate and consistent.
- Manage and mentor the Safety Managers and Safety Associates in your assigned site.
- Engage the Injury Prevention Specialists (IPS) and Site Leadership to drive long-term strategic actions to achieve incident reduction.
- Perform targeted Kaizen events in partnership with the Operations teams based on the risks identified in each task (force, repetition, and awkward postures).
- Ensure site leadership and associates are trained and knowledgeable of their responsibilities under each policy.
- Audit the quality, delivery (including qualifications of the trainer), and effectiveness of all required safety training.
- Review for effectiveness the deployed safety tools and revise to ensure continual improvement.
- Partner with corporate and other regional field safety personnel to leverage global safety and environmental best practices into NA network standards.

Additional Job Elements include:
- Lift up to 49 pounds and frequently push, pull, squat, bend, and reach
- Stand/walk for up to 12 hours during shifts
- Work in an environment where the noise level varies
- Work in an environment that is subject to variable temperatures and weather (delivery stations include outside loading departments)
- Continuously climb and descend stairs (applies to sites with stairs)
- Maintain effective care delivery in emergencies and assist emergency response at the site

Those that do not have an adult First Aid, CPR, AED certification from the American Heart Association or American Red Cross must obtain within 3 weeks of start date.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree
- 7+ years of increasing responsibilities in safety and/or environmental programs in manufacturing, production, or service operations, or relevant experience applicable to the role
- 7+ years of increasing responsibilities in people and performance management
- Experience implementing lean principles and process improvement in an operational environment
- Willingness to work a variety of shifts, including nights and weekends, as required to support direct reports and site needs

Preferred qualifications

- Master’s degree preferred
- Certified Safety Professional preferred
- Experience in a fast-paced, dynamic organization
- Interest in long-term career development through assignments in multiple business units across the nation
- Prior experience in a management development training program
- Track record of effectively managing a safety operation comprising both salaried and hourly staff
- Demonstrate experience in developing others into higher levels of responsibility in an organization
- Strong written and verbal communication skills, including comfort interfacing with Directors and VPs
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills

title: Logistics Specialist,
descriptionHtml:
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of the data centers that power AWS. As a Logistics Specialist on the Data Center Materials team in Kuala Lumpur, you'll help keep our data centers supplied with the hardware and materials they need to run reliably for our customers.

In this role, you'll manage the flow of materials across our KUL sites, including receiving, storing, tracking, and shipping servers, racks, cables, optics, and spare parts. You'll keep inventory records accurate, run cycle counts, and work with vendors, carriers, and internal teams to make sure parts arrive on time for rack deployments and repairs. You'll also help with inbound and outbound shipments, customs documentation, and the disposition of decommissioned equipment.

This is a hands-on role in a fast-paced environment where priorities can change quickly. You'll spot problems early, take ownership of fixing them, and look for ways to improve how we work. You'll work closely with Data Center Operations, Procurement, and Supply Chain teams, and build skills in data center logistics and inventory management along the way.

Key job responsibilities
Receive, inspect, store, and ship data center hardware and materials
Maintain accurate inventory records in our inventory systems and run regular cycle counts
Track orders and shipments, and follow up with vendors and carriers to meet delivery timelines
Prepare shipping and customs documentation for inbound and outbound shipments
Support rack deployments and repairs by making sure the right parts are available onsite
Handle disposition of decommissioned and defective equipment according to AWS standards
Follow safety, security, and compliance procedures at all times
Identify process gaps and suggest improvements to make the team more efficient

A day in the life
This position works in-person at a data center site. A typical day includes:
Processing inbound shipments — unpacking, verifying contents against POs, updating inventory systems, and staging parts for distribution
Fulfilling parts requests from Data Center Technicians and Engineers, and transporting equipment between locations
Performing data entry, updating inventory records, and resolving queries from peer organisations
Maintaining up-to-date metrics dashboards, spreadsheets, and preparing reports for internal/external customers and management as required
Scheduling deliveries and pick-ups to and from production locations
Validating billing associated with the inventory supply chain to ensure accuracy and readiness for processing
Keeping precise records of all commodities entering and leaving the facility
Shifting priorities as needed without friction to support operational demands

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree or equivalent qualification in supply chain management, engineering, business management or other relevant field. Fresh graduates are welcome and encouraged to apply
- Proficient in Microsoft Excel or similar tools for tracking and reporting data
- Clear written and verbal communication in English
- Able to work onsite in a data center, including lifting up to 23 kg (50 lbs) and standing or walking for long period

Preferred qualifications

- Familiar with computer hardware components (such as servers, cables, and optics) and operating systems
- Understanding of shipping, receiving, and customs clearance processes
- Strong attention to detail and good organizational skills, with the ability to handle several priorities at once

title: Sr. SDM, Device and Partner Qualification, Amazon Leo, D2D Software
descriptionHtml:
Description
Amazon Leo is building a low Earth orbit satellite constellation to bring fast, affordable connectivity to customers around the world. Direct to Device (D2D) extends Leo to standard mobile phones and devices: a fully regenerative fifth-generation (5G) mobile base station on each satellite, delivering service to standard handsets through mobile network operators (MNOs). D2D Software builds the embedded software that flies, the cloud and ground software that runs the service, and the platform that connects them. Our target is under a day from a defect being found to the fix deployed across the entire constellation, achieved by automating everything that a person would otherwise do by hand.

This role leads device and partner qualification in Software Integration, Verification & Reliability, reporting to the Director, Software Integration, Verification & Reliability. It owns interoperability requirements, qualification kits, conformance and certification, and supplier contract test suites. Before anything is handed on, the bar is: qualification kits published for every device class. It hands off to its customers as follows: qualification verdicts to Customer and operators.

What the team needs to achieve
• Qualification kits published for every device class.
• Hand-offs that meet their service level: qualification verdicts to Customer and operators.
• Measured, rising capability and efficiency of the team, with manual work falling release over release.

How the team is measured
• Qualification cycle time, release over release.
• Device issues found after qualification.

Export Control Requirement:
Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.


Key job responsibilities
• Own interoperability requirements, qualification kits, conformance and certification, and supplier contract test suites.
• Meet the bar before every hand-off: qualification kits published for every device class.
• Work directly with engineers in the boundary teams as partners, through agreed contracts and service levels.
• Automate everything a person would otherwise do twice.
• Hire, coach, and grow the team, with clear expectations and career development for every engineer.
• Define the team's metrics and service levels, and improve them release over release.
• Make the team's decisions data-driven and its quality measurable, and escalate early when risks cross team boundaries.
• Set the team's roadmap and the structure and mechanisms that deliver it, and negotiate the boundaries of the area with peer teams.
• Build the mechanisms and best practices that make the team's work repeatable, measurable, and improving.



A day in the life



About the team
D2D Software is an evolving organization of many teams: Software Architecture & Specifications; Software Delivery & Business Ops; Software Integration, Verification & Reliability; DevOps & Release; Satellite Software Development; Ground Software Development; and Customer Software Engineering & Support. Each Director owns business outcomes: delivering the commitments, and the capability and efficiency of their teams. Teams work as internal customers and suppliers with agreed service levels, interfaces are agreed centrally while designs stay local, and engineers are expected to work directly with engineers across every boundary. Milestones are committed deadlines for delivery with quality, not gates to wait on, and every team runs on one toolchain and one system of record. Every measure is derived from the systems of record, never self-reported, and we improve release over release with a target of perfection.

- 5+ years of software development experience, including experience managing a team of engineers
- Experience hiring and developing engineers, setting clear goals, and giving regular feedback and coaching
- Experience establishing workflows, metrics, and service levels for a team, and making data-driven trade-offs between short- and long-term needs
- Experience leading a team where the problem and strategy are not yet fully defined, working backwards from the customer
- Experience qualifying devices, chipsets, or networks against standards and certification schemes
- Experience building qualification kits and interoperability test suites
- Experience across the full software development lifecycle, having shipped software and maintained it in production

Preferred qualifications

- Experience with non-terrestrial network devices
- Experience managing managers or leading several teams
- Experience setting a multi-year direction for an area, designing the team structure and mechanisms to deliver it, and aligning several teams around it
- Experience setting strategy where the problem, opportunity, and strategy are not defined, telling one-way from two-way doors, and presenting decisions and strategy narratives to senior leaders across the organization
- A record of writing clear narratives and running data-driven reviews

They provide 24/7 shift coverage which could include 12 hour shifts, rotating shifts, 3, 4, or 5 day work weeks.

This position requires that the candidate selected be a US citizen and possess and maintain an active TS/SCI security clearance with polygraph.

Key job responsibilities
- Operate and maintain mechanical and electrical, mechanical, emergency generator, and fire/life safety equipment within the data center

- Perform limited maintenance tasks to including filter changes, HVAC PMs, rack power installs, rack PDU, and rack ATS replacements
- Provide support to Data Center Operations technicians
- Perform root cause analysis of equipment failures

- Regularly lift and/or move up to 39 pounds; and participate in group lifts for 40 pounds or more
- Bend or twist the body into unusual positions while working
- Push or pull heavy objects into position
- Work in noisy environments

About the team
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Our teams build and operate scalable solutions across a wide range of functions, with a focus on customer experience, operational excellence, innovation, and continuous improvement. Employees work in a fast-paced environment, partnering across teams and geographies to solve complex business problems and deliver results at scale.
Operations as a Service (OaaS enables the business to deliver products and services to customers across the globe. Our teams manage complex, high-volume processes and continuously improve how work is executed through standardization, technology, data, and automation. The role offers an opportunity to work across teams and geographies, solve operational challenges, and drive improvements at scale.


Key job responsibilities
• Process Transition: Collaborate with the Transition team suppory process onboarding, , SOP creation, training, and ramp-up to enable transition to BAU.
• Process Expertise & Execution: Develop deep process expertise and independently execute test and production cases. Serve as the subject matter expert for assigned workflows and provide guidance to Operations.
• Program Governance & Performance: Establish mechanisms to track SLA, TPH, quality, TAT, backlog, and other key metrics. Analyze performance trends and provide insights for WBRs, MBRs, QBRs, and business decisions.
• Stakeholder Management: Act as the primary process POC and partner with business stakeholders and internal teams, including Operations, STL, Transition, CPT, and ONT, to align requirements, manage dependencies, and drive execution.
• Problem Solving & Escalation Management: Own critical process issues, conduct root-cause analysis, and implement corrective and preventive actions. Identify systemic gaps and drive resolution with partner teams.
• Process Excellence & Simplification: Identify process inefficiencies, standardize workflows, and drive best practices across programs. Build reporting and communication mechanisms to improve performance visibility.
• Automation & Scalability: Identify opportunities to eliminate manual effort and improve process scalability. Partner with Tech and Operations teams to design and implement automation and other process improvements.
• Flexibility to work in 24x7 shift and rotational weekly off

Basic qualifications

- Experience communicating with a wide range of stakeholders, including colleagues and leadership, or experience in an operational role

Preferred qualifications

- Experience working with MS Excel, VBA, SQL, Data Warehouse or business intelligence systems and data visualization tools such as Tableau
